# GitHub Discussions Setup Guide for Midori

This guide explains how to set up and manage GitHub Discussions for Midori Browser to build an active, welcoming community.

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Category Setup](#category-setup)
- [Community Guidelines](#community-guidelines)
- [Moderation Best Practices](#moderation-best-practices)
- [Engagement Strategy](#engagement-strategy)

---

## Overview

GitHub Discussions provide a space for the Midori community to:

✅ **Ask questions** without opening formal issues  
✅ **Share ideas** and get feedback  
✅ **Discuss features** before implementation  
✅ **Show off projects** using Midori  
✅ **Network** with other users and contributors  

Discussions are more conversational than Issues and help build community.

---

## Category Setup

Set up the following discussion categories (via Repository → Settings → Discussions):

### 1. 🎉 Announcements

**Purpose:** Official news, releases, and major updates

**Guidelines:**
- Posts limited to maintainers
- Used for release notes, roadmap updates, security notices
- Auto-close after 30 days

**Example threads:**
- "Midori 2.0 Released! 🚀"
- "Security Update Available"
- "2026 Q2 Roadmap"

---

### 2. 💬 General Discussion

**Purpose:** Off-topic chat, general conversation

**Guidelines:**
- Users share feedback, ideas, and stories
- Help from community members
- Discovery of how people use Midori

**Example threads:**
- "What features do you use most in Midori?"
- "My Midori customization setup"
- "Privacy tips and tricks"

---

### 3. ❓ Getting Help

**Purpose:** User support and troubleshooting

**Guidelines:**
- For usage questions and setup help
- Community + maintainers answer
- Link to official docs
- Redirect serious bugs to issues

**Example threads:**
- "How do I export my bookmarks?"
- "Sync not working on my Mac"
- "Can I use Midori extensions?"

---

### 4. 🤔 Q&A (Question & Answer)

**Purpose:** Technical questions with structured answers

**Guidelines:**
- Use voting to highlight best answers
- Maintainers mark correct solutions
- Discoverable for future users

**Example threads:**
- "How do I build Midori from source?"
- "Best practices for browser extensions"
- "Recommended privacy settings"

---

### 5. 💡 Ideas

**Purpose:** Feature requests and brainstorming

**Guidelines:**
- Pre-proposal discussions (before issues)
- Community feedback on viability
- Gather requirements together
- Link to formal issue when ready

**Example threads:**
- "What about tab groups?"
- "Built-in email client?"
- "Enhanced ad blocker settings"

---

### 6. 🎨 Showcase

**Purpose:** Show off projects, extensions, and customizations

**Guidelines:**
- Community highlights their work
- Celebrate creativity and innovation
- Link to repos, demos, blogs
- Monthly community spotlight

**Example threads:**
- "I built a Midori theme!"
- "My Midori extension: Password Manager Plus"
- "Midori on my Linux setup"

---

### 7. 🐛 Bugs

**Purpose:** Report and discuss bugs (before formal issues)

**Guidelines:**
- Triage bugs together
- Confirm reproducibility with community
- Maintainers convert to formal issues
- Link to issue when created

**Example threads:**
- "Crash on startup with certain settings"
- "Memory leak in New Tab page"
- "Bookmark sync delays"

---

### 8. 🧑‍💻 Development

**Purpose:** Developer discussions, architecture, technical deep-dives

**Guidelines:**
- Code reviews and improvements
- Architecture discussions
- Pull request discussions
- Build system troubleshooting

**Example threads:**
- "Improving Midori's sync performance"
- "New Tab page refactoring ideas"
- "Benchmarking extension loading"

---

### 9. 🌍 Community & Events

**Purpose:** Meetups, conferences, contests, community initiatives

**Guidelines:**
- Organize events
- Share conference talks
- Contest announcements
- Community milestones

**Example threads:**
- "Midori Community Meetup - May 15"
- "We're at FOSDEM 2026!"
- "First 10K GitHub Stars! 🎉"

---

## Community Guidelines

### Before Starting a Discussion

- 🔍 **Search first** — Your question might already be answered
- 📝 **Be specific** — Include context and details
- 🙏 **Be respectful** — Treat others with kindness
- 📸 **Show effort** — Share what you've already tried

### Writing Good Discussions

**Title:** Clear, specific, searchable
```
❌ "Help"
✅ "How do I sync bookmarks between devices?"
```

**Body:** Include context
```markdown
I'm using Midori 1.5 on Windows 11. 
I've enabled sync in settings, but bookmarks aren't appearing on my Mac.

What I've tried:
- Restarted the app
- Checked sync is enabled on both devices

Any ideas?
```

**Code formatting:** Use syntax highlighting
````markdown
```javascript
// Your code here
const result = await sync.fetch();
```
````

## Moderation Best Practices

### Daily Tasks

- ⭐ **Welcome new users** — Reply to first posts
- 🏆 **Mark helpful answers** — Use the "Mark as answer" button
- 📌 **Pin important threads** — Keep them visible
- 🗑️ **Remove spam** — Use moderation tools

### Weekly Tasks

- 📊 **Review trends** — What topics are most discussed?
- 🎯 **Respond to unanswered** — Ensure people get help
- 👥 **Feature contributors** — Highlight helpful community members
- 📈 **Track growth** — Monitor participation metrics

### Monthly Tasks

- 🎉 **Community spotlight** — Highlight best threads/contributors
- 🗺️ **Update FAQs** — Common questions → pinned thread
- 📋 **Review moderation** — Ensure policies are working
- 🚀 **Promote to users** — Share discussion highlights on social media

### Moderation Actions

**Lock discussions:** When off-topic or heated
```
We're going to lock this discussion as it's moving away from Midori Browser.
Please open a new discussion if you have Midori-specific questions!
```

**Move to issues:** When it's actually a bug
```
Thanks for reporting this! This looks like a bug.
I'm opening an issue to track it: #1234
Please reply there if you have additional details.
```

**Redirect to docs:** For FAQ questions
```
Great question! This is covered in our docs:
👉 [Link to docs]

Feel free to ask if something's unclear!
```

## Engagement Strategy

### Get Initial Traction

1. **Seed discussions** (maintainers start threads)
   - Ask the community about priorities
   - Share behind-the-scenes stories
   - Announce new features in real-time

2. **Cross-promote** (other channels)
   - Link to discussions from Twitter/Reddit
   - Mention in releases
   - Share in emails/newsletters

3. **Incentivize participation** (early adopters)
   - Spotlight contributors
   - Feature community projects
   - Monthly raffle prizes (stickers, merchandise)

### Build Participation

**Monthly Themes:**
```
Week 1: Monday Feature Spotlight
Week 2: User Stories & Showcases
Week 3: Developer Q&A
Week 4: Ideas & Feature Requests
```

**Community Events:**
- 🎤 Monthly live chat (Telegram + stream)
- 📚 Weekly dev deep-dives
- 🏆 Monthly contributor spotlight
- 🎁 Quarterly contests (screenshot, extension, blog post)

### Highlight Success Stories

**Monthly Spotlight Post:**
```markdown
# 🌟 Community Spotlight - May 2026

Thanks to our amazing community! Here are this month's highlights:

## Best Answer
@contributor_name answered 47 questions in Getting Help!
👉 [Top answer link]

## Best Showcase
@someone_awesome shared their beautiful Midori theme!
👉 [Showcase thread]

## Best Idea
Discussion about tab groups got 50+ upvotes
👉 [Ideas thread]

Keep being awesome! 💚
```

## Automation

### GitHub Actions for Discussions

Consider these automations:

**Auto-respond to first posts:**
```yaml
name: Welcome to Discussions
on:
  discussion:
    types: [created]

jobs:
  welcome:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Comment on new discussion
        run: |
          # Greet user and link to guidelines
```

**Lock old discussions:**
```yaml
- name: Lock old discussions
  if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
  run: |
    # Lock discussions older than 90 days (if no activity)
```

**Create weekly threads:**
```yaml
- name: Create weekly developer Q&A
  if: github.event.schedule == '0 9 * * 3'  # Wednesday 9 AM
  run: |
    # Auto-create weekly thread
```

## Metrics & Reporting

### Track Success

Monitor these metrics:

| Metric | Target | Frequency |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| Discussions created/week | 20+ | Weekly |
| Replies per discussion | 3+ | Monthly |
| Unanswered threads | <10% | Weekly |
| Community answers | >50% | Monthly |
| New members engaged | +5-10/week | Weekly |

**Dashboard:** Create a simple report (monthly):
```
May 2026 Discussion Metrics
- Total discussions: 156 (↑ 15%)
- Total replies: 487 (↑ 25%)
- Unanswered: 8% (↓ 2%)
- New members: 32
- Top contributors: @username1, @username2, @username3
```
